newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PLO's Husseini makes last-minute settlements plea.
newsitem.headline: PLO's Husseini makes last-minute settlements plea.

text.p: Faisal al-Husseini, the top PLO official in Jerusalem, visited Israel's parliament on Wednesday and made a last-minute appeal to the Jewish state to scrap a plan to build a new Jewish neighbourhood in Arab East Jerusalem.

"I would like to say that my coming here to this place is because we would like to defend this peace process," Husseini said beneath a portrait of Yitzhak Rabin, the Israeli prime minister assassinated in 1995 by a right-wing Jew for handing over occupied West Bank lands to the Palestinians.

"A lot of Israelis and Palestinians gave their lives for this peace process, including Yitzhak Rabin," said Husseini, who was invited to parliament by left-wing legislators for meetings outside the plenum.

His visit came hours before Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu was set to approve a plan to build 6,500 homes for Jews on Har Homa, called Jabal Abu Ghneim by Arabs, a tree-covered hill taken by Israel in the 1967 Middle East war.
"What the Israeli government is doing here at Jabal Abu Ghneim and other places...can destroy everything," Husseini said. "Everything is ready for an explosion."

Left-wing Israeli lawmakers urged Netanyahu not to approve the Har Homa plan in order to prevent clashes like those sparked last September when Netanyahu opened an entrance to a tunnel near Moslem holy sites in Jerusalem. Sixty-one Arabs and 15 Israelis were killed in the violence.
"We don't want another tunnel," Labour party lawmaker Yael Dayan told reporters.

Husseini, whose PLO East Jerusalem headquarters at Orient House is seen by many Jews as a threat to Israel's sovereignty in the city's occupied eastern half, said unilateral Israeli actions in Jerusalem violated interim peace deals.
Palestinians want East Jerusalem as the capital of a future state. Israel says all of the city is its "eternal" capital, a claim not recognised internationally.

Interim Israeli-PLO peace deals left the status of Jerusalem, one of the most sensitive issues in the Arab-Israel conflict, for talks on the final status of the West Bank and Gaza Strip which must be completed by 1999.
